return this.http.get(this.hostServer + '/rest/user/change-password?current=' + passwords.current + '&new=' +
    passwords.new + '&repeat=' + passwords.repeat).pipe(map((response: any) => response.user), catchError((err) => { throw err.error }))

context.guidance: Keep Personal Data out of application, access and error logs. Write an opaque identifier or a masked form in place of each value, and strip request bodies and query strings before a log line is written. Where a value must be recorded, apply a protection that Rule 6(1)(a) names, such as encryption, obfuscation, masking or a virtual token. Apply the same rule to logging middleware and to any external log sink.

value.fix: Stop sending passwords in the URL. Change the call to a POST (or PUT) with the values in the JSON request body: `this.http.post(this.hostServer + '/rest/user/change-password', { current: passwords.current, new: passwords.new, repeat: passwords.repeat }).pipe(map((response: any) => response.user), catchError((err) => { throw err.error }))`. Query strings are written to access logs, proxy logs, and browser history, so the credentials currently leak there. On the server, configure the logging middleware and any external log sink to drop request bodies and query strings before writing a line. Where a value must appear in a log, mask it (for example, `***`) or replace it with an opaque identifier. Also make sure the error handler does not log or return the raw `err.error` payload when it might echo submitted values. Finally, confirm the change by sending a password-change request and checking that the access log line, error log line, and external sink contain no password values or query-string parameters.
